title: SUMONE: A Simple and Efficient Summarizer for Plug-and-Play Agent Memory
title_zh: SUMONE：面向即插即用智能体记忆的简单高效摘要器

paragraphs.en: Long-horizon language-model agents accumulate increasingly large interaction histories, making context compaction essential for efficient execution. Existing learned compaction methods often rely on downstream task outcomes or solver behavior, coupling training to specific tasks or agents. We introduce SumOne, a standalone summarizer trained to preserve information in agent histories through masked reconstruction. Given a summary of the expired history, a frozen reconstructor recovers randomly masked portions of the original trajectory; reconstruction quality, combined with a length penalty, provides a task-agnostic reward for optimizing the summarizer with GRPO. This yields self-supervision directly from raw trajectories, without reference summaries or downstream task execution. At inference time, only the lightweight summarizer is retained, enabling plug-and-play context compression for otherwise unchanged agents. We conduct a systematic evaluation of SumOne in long-horizon search and software-engineering tasks. SumOne reduces estimated inference cost by approximately 78% on DeepSearchQA and 75% on SWE-bench Verified relative to operating with full context, with absolute decreases of 0.04. The same checkpoint also transfers across downstream models and agent harnesses without additional fine-tuning.

paragraphs.en: Large language models are increasingly used to build agents that reason over multiple steps, call tools, and respond to observations from an external environment ( Yao et al., 2023 ; OpenAI, 2025 ; Anthropic, 2026 ; Kimi Team et al., 2026 ) . Such agents need access to earlier interactions: a search agent may have to combine evidence found at different steps, while a coding agent may need to recall a user constraint, a previous code change, or the outcome of a failed test. As the task continues, these interactions accumulate into a long trajectory. Passing the entire trajectory to the model increases inference cost and eventually reaches its context limit ( Liu et al., 2024 ; Su et al., 2024 ) . Yet keeping every interaction verbatim is often unnecessary. Tool outputs contain irrelevant details, and the outcome of a completed step may be more useful than its full sequence of actions. The challenge is therefore to reduce the context the agent reads without discarding information it may need later ( Hu et al., 2025b ) .
paragraphs.zh: 大语言模型越来越多地被用于构建能够进行多步推理、调用工具并响应外部环境观测的智能体（Yao et al., 2023；OpenAI, 2025；Anthropic, 2026；Kimi Team et al., 2026）。 这类智能体需要访问早期的交互内容：搜索智能体可能需要整合在不同步骤中找到的证据，而编程智能体可能需要回想起某个用户约束、之前的一次代码改动或某次失败测试的结果。 随着任务的持续进行，这些交互会累积成一条长长的轨迹。 将整条轨迹传给模型会增加推理成本，并最终达到模型的上下文上限（Liu et al., 2024；Su et al., 2024）。 然而，逐字保留每一次交互往往是不必要的。 工具输出中包含无关细节，而一个已完成步骤的结果可能比其完整的动作序列更有用。 因此，挑战在于在不丢弃智能体后续可能需要的信息的前提下，缩减智能体所读取的上下文（Hu et al., 2025b）。

paragraphs.en: Existing approaches to agent context management can be roughly organized into three groups. The first uses prompting or simple rules to shorten the context, for example, by discarding older interactions or asking a model to summarize them. Automatic compaction in Codex and Claude Code shows the practical value of this approach ( Pathak and Fabbri, 2026 ; Anthropic, ) . The second group ties memory management to the agent’s task or training process. HiAgent summarizes completed subgoals within the agent workflow; FoldGRPO trains agents to operate with compressed tool responses; ( Hu et al., 2025a ; Sun and others, 2025 ) . These methods can adapt memory to the decisions an agent must make, but their design or training depends on a particular task workflow or downstream solver. The third group provides more general memory frameworks. A-MEM ( Xu et al., 2026 ) , for instance, manages information across context and external storage, with explicit decisions about what to retain and retrieve. Such frameworks offer a broader memory interface, but also require the agent to additionally interact with that interface.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的智能体上下文管理方法大致可以分为三类。 第一类使用提示词或简单规则来缩短上下文，例如丢弃较早的交互内容，或要求模型对它们进行总结。 Codex 和 Claude Code 中的自动压缩展示了这一方法的实用价值（Pathak and Fabbri, 2026；Anthropic,）。 第二类将记忆管理与智能体的任务或训练过程绑定在一起。 HiAgent 在智能体工作流内总结已完成的子目标；FoldGRPO 训练智能体在压缩后的工具响应下运行（Hu et al., 2025a；Sun and others, 2025）。 这些方法能够让记忆适应智能体必须做出的决策，但它们的设计或训练依赖于特定的任务工作流或下游求解器。 第三类提供了更通用的记忆框架。 例如，A-MEM（Xu et al., 2026）在上下文与外部存储之间管理信息，并显式地决定保留和检索哪些内容。 这类框架提供了更广泛的记忆接口，但也要求智能体额外与该接口进行交互。

paragraphs.en: Together, these approaches leave room for a memory mechanism that is agnostic to specific tasks, lightweight to use, while maintaining high information density. We propose to train a dedicated small language model that compresses running context of other agents, only using raw trajectories. However, the central challenge would be the training signal. Given a long agent trajectory and its compressed version, how should one judge its completeness and compactness? In this paper, we use masked reconstruction, a classic training objective in self-supervised learning ( Lewis et al., 2020 ; He et al., 2022 ) , as a proxy to assess what a summary preserves. Given a summary of trajectory segments, we first mask parts of the original trajectory, and adopt a frozen model to predict the complete history. As a result, the overlap between the original trajectory and the prediction provides a training signal derived from the data itself, without external references or downstream task execution.
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，这些方法为一种记忆机制留下了空间：该机制不依赖特定任务、使用轻量，同时保持高信息密度。 我们提出训练一个专用的小型语言模型，仅使用原始轨迹来压缩其他智能体的运行上下文。 然而，核心挑战在于训练信号。 给定一条长的智能体轨迹及其压缩版本，应如何评判其完整性与紧凑性？ 在本文中，我们使用掩码重建——自监督学习中的经典训练目标（Lewis et al., 2020; He et al., 2022）——作为评估摘要保留了多少信息的代理指标。 给定轨迹片段的摘要，我们首先遮蔽原始轨迹的部分内容，然后采用一个冻结的模型来预测完整的历史。 由此，原始轨迹与预测之间的重叠提供了源自数据本身的训练信号，无需外部参考或下游任务执行。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate SumOne on long-horizon search and software-engineering tasks, together with agentic memory benchmarks and transfer across downstream agents and harnesses. On DeepSearchQA ( Gupta et al., 2026 ) , SumOne reduces more than 70% cumulative agent input and 77% end-to-end task cost per query compared to evaluating with full context, while causing merely 0.04 drop in F1 score. On SWE-bench Verified ( Jimenez et al., 2024a ) , it achieves a 59% resolved rate versus 63%, while reducing input from 4.1M to 1.09M tokens per task. Compared with agent self-summarization, SumOne performs better on both benchmarks while using notably less end-to-end cost,with Figure 1(b) highlighting the results for SWE-bench Verified. It also achieves the strongest results among compression methods on LongMemEval-S ( Wu et al., 2025 ) and transfers across multiple downstream LLMs and agent harnesses without additional fine-tuning.

paragraphs.en: Our broader aim is to make memory management a capability of a dedicated module that can serve different agents, similar to the role that hippocampus plays in human brains ( McClelland et al., 1995 ) . SumOne addresses one part of this problem: learning to write compact memory from raw interaction histories, with supervision obtained from the data itself. paragraphs.en: Tool-using agents accumulate long histories of actions and observations ( Yao et al., 2023 ) , motivating mechanisms for retaining useful information under limited context budgets. Existing approaches can be broadly grouped into three categories. First , input-level compression reduces context by selecting, removing, or masking parts of the original input, rather than synthesizing a new memory representation, as in prompt compression ( Jiang et al., 2023 ; Pan and others, 2024 ) and observation masking ( Lindenbauer et al., 2025 ) . Second , agent-managed compaction incorporates memory maintenance into the agent workflow, such as subgoal summarization in HiAgent ( Hu et al., 2025a ) and learned context folding ( Sun and others, 2025 ; Ye and others, 2025 ) . Third , standalone summarization methods compress interaction histories into textual memory for subsequent agent execution. Methods ( Wu and others, 2025 ; Kang and others, 2025 ; Zhang and others, 2026 ) in this category typically tie the learning or evaluation of summaries to downstream task outcomes or solver behavior. SumOne also adopts a standalone summarizer, but learns it with a task-agnostic reconstruction objective.
paragraphs.zh: 使用工具的智能体会积累冗长的动作与观察历史（Yao 等， 2023），这促使人们设计在有限上下文预算下保留有用信息的机制。 现有方法可以大致分为三类。 第一类是输入级压缩，通过选择、删除或遮蔽原始输入的部分内容来缩减上下文，而不是合成新的记忆表示，例如提示压缩（Jiang 等， 2023；Pan 等， 2024）和观察遮蔽（Lindenbauer 等， 2025）。 第二类是智能体自主管理的压缩，将记忆维护纳入智能体工作流中，例如 HiAgent 中的子目标摘要（Hu 等， 2025a）以及学习到的上下文折叠（Sun 等， 2025；Ye 等， 2025）。 第三类是独立摘要方法，将交互历史压缩为文本记忆，供后续智能体执行使用。 这一类别中的方法（Wu 等， 2025；Kang 等， 2025；Zhang 等， 2026）通常将摘要的学习或评估与下游任务结果或求解器行为绑定。 SumOne 同样采用独立的摘要器，但通过一个与任务无关的重构目标来学习它。

paragraphs.en: We introduce SumOne , a framework for learning compact agent memories without relying on downstream task execution as supervision. Our key idea is to treat summarization as information-preserving compression : a good summary should retain information from the expired interaction history that remains useful after the original history is discarded. To train for this property directly, SumOne generates a summary of the expired history (Section 3.1 ), masks part of the original history, and asks a frozen reconstructor to recover the missing content from the summary and retained context (Section 3.2 ). Reconstruction quality is then converted into a reward for optimizing the summarizer with GRPO ( Shao et al., 2024 ) (Section 3.3 ). At inference time, the reconstruction pipeline is removed, leaving only the lightweight summarizer as a plug-and-play context compression module (Section 3.4 ).
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出 SumOne，一个用于学习紧凑智能体记忆的框架，它不依赖下游任务执行作为监督信号。 我们的核心思路是将摘要视为信息保持压缩：一个好的摘要应当保留已过期交互历史中的信息，使得在原始历史被丢弃后，这些信息仍然有用。 为了直接训练这一特性，SumOne 对已过期历史生成摘要（第 3.1 节），掩盖原始历史的一部分，并要求一个冻结的重构器根据摘要和保留的上下文恢复缺失内容（第 3.2 节）。 重构质量随后被转化为奖励，用于通过 GRPO（Shao et al., 2024）优化摘要器（第 3.3 节）。 在推理时，重构流程被移除，仅保留轻量级摘要器作为一个即插即用的上下文压缩模块（第 3.4 节）。

paragraphs.en: Our primary agent benchmarks are DeepSearchQA ( Gupta et al., 2026 ) for web search and SWE-bench Verified ( Jimenez et al., 2024b ) for software engineering; we additionally use LongMemEval-S for isolated memory evaluation. paragraphs.en: SumOne retains most of the Full History performance at a fraction of the cost. Table 1 reports the main results on DeepSearchQA and SWE-bench Verified, using Qwen3.5-35B-A3B as the downstream agent with OpenCode as the agent harness. On DeepSearchQA, SumOne achieves 0.48 F1 compared with 0.52 for Full History, while reducing cumulative agent input from 2.83M to 591K tokens and requiring only 22% of the total inference cost of Full History. These results show that SumOne preserves most of the utility of the full interaction history with a substantially smaller context and cost footprint.

paragraphs.en: SumOne provides a better performance–cost trade-off than existing summarization approaches. On DeepSearchQA, SumOne improves over Self-Summary from 0.44 to 0.48 F1 while requiring only 0.04 × 0.04\times the summarization cost and 0.86 × 0.86\times the total inference cost. On SWE-bench Verified, SumOne similarly improves the resolved rate from 0.56 to 0.59, using only 0.08 × 0.08\times the summarization cost and 0.86 × 0.86\times the total inference cost of Self-Summary. SumOne also consistently outperforms Prompt-2B under comparable compression and achieves stronger overall performance than CoMem across the two tasks. The substantial improvement over Prompt-2B suggests that simply replacing self-summarization with a lightweight standalone model is insufficient; reconstruction-based training enables the summarizer to preserve information that is more useful for subsequent agent execution.

paragraphs.en: SumOne preserves more generally accessible information for subsequent retrieval and reasoning. While Section 4.2 evaluates compression through downstream agent performance, here we further decouple memory quality from task execution using LongMemEval-S , which directly evaluates long-term memory capabilities. As shown in Table 4 , the overall performance follows Oracle > > Full History > > SumOne > > Prompt-2B > > CoMem . In contrast, SumOne maintains competitive performance across single-session retrieval, multi-session reasoning, temporal reasoning, and knowledge updates. This more balanced behavior is consistent with our task-agnostic reconstruction objective, which encourages broad information preservation rather than optimizing memory toward a particular downstream task or capability.

paragraphs.en: A moderate mask ratio yields better performance. We study the effect of the reconstruction mask ratio in Table 6(a) . A mask ratio of 50% performs best on both DeepSearchQA and LongMemEval-S, achieving 48% and 7%, respectively. Reducing the mask ratio to 25% weakens the reconstruction objective: since much of the original trajectory remains directly observable, the reconstructor relies less on the summary, resulting in a weaker learning signal for the summarizer. In contrast, increasing the mask ratio to 75% substantially degrades performance, likely because recovering such a large portion of the trajectory becomes overly challenging for the reconstructor and consequently introduces a noisier training signal. These results suggest that masking roughly half of the expired history provides a better balance between reconstruction difficulty and supervision quality.

paragraphs.en: A moderate length penalty balances well between compression and information preservation. We study the effect of the length-penalty coefficient λ \lambda in Equation 6 , with results reported in Table 6(b) . A moderate value of λ = 0.1 \lambda=0.1 performs best on both DeepSearchQA and LongMemEval-S. In contrast, stronger penalties ( λ = 0.2 \lambda=0.2 or 0.5 0.5 ) encourage overly aggressive compression, causing useful information to be discarded and degrading downstream performance.

sents.zh: 当惩罚过弱（λ = 0.01 \lambda=0.01）时，总结器受到的约束不足，倾向于产生不必要的长摘要，降低了压缩效率却没有带来相应的性能提升。

sents.en: In contrast, stronger penalties ( λ = 0.2 \lambda=0.2 or 0.5 0.5 ) encourage overly aggressive compression, causing useful information to be discarded and degrading downstream performance.
sents.zh: 相反，更强的惩罚（λ = 0.2 \lambda=0.2 或 0.5 0.5）会促使过度激进的压缩，导致有用信息被丢弃，从而降低下游性能。

paragraphs.en: While SumOne demonstrates that masked reconstruction provides an effective task-agnostic signal for learning compact agent memory, several limitations remain. First, our training data are concentrated in web-search and software-engineering trajectories, and broader domains may exhibit different memory requirements. Second, the training signal depends on a frozen reconstructor and an LLM-based reconstruction judge; although neither is needed at inference time, their capabilities may affect the quality of the learned summarizer. For future work, extending the module with adaptive memory management, retrieval, tools, and meta-memory is a promising direction toward a more complete agent memory system.

paragraphs.en: We introduced SumOne , a lightweight plug-and-play summarizer for compressing long agent interaction histories. Rather than supervising summaries through downstream task outcomes or reference summaries, SumOne learns directly from raw trajectories by rewarding summaries that enable masked portions of the original history to be reconstructed, while regularizing summary length. Across long-horizon search, software engineering, and direct memory evaluation, SumOne substantially reduces context consumption while retaining most of the utility of full interaction histories, and transfers across downstream models and agent harnesses without additional fine-tuning. These results suggest that reconstruction-based self-supervision offers a simple and general route toward reusable memory modules for long-running language-model agents.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 SumOne，一个轻量级即插即用的摘要器，用于压缩智能体交互历史。 SumOne 不通过下游任务结果或参考摘要来监督摘要，而是直接从原始轨迹中学习，奖励那些能够重建原始历史中被遮蔽部分的摘要，同时对摘要长度进行正则化。 在长程搜索、软件工程和直接记忆评估中，SumOne 在保留完整交互历史大部分效用的同时大幅降低了上下文消耗，并且无需额外微调即可在不同下游模型和智能体框架之间迁移。 这些结果表明，基于重建的自监督为长期运行的语言模型智能体提供了一条简单而通用的路径，以构建可复用的记忆模块。
